decision_register.summary: The Mermaid `flowchart TD` with nodes in the same subgraph is the root cause — design/explore/planning share horizontal space and arrows between them inherently cross. The only real solution is to separate `design` and `explore` into their own subgraph so they can be positioned independently of `planning`. Here's the fix: split L2 into two parallel subgraphs — one for the design/explore cluster and one for planning — keeping them both at the same vertical level but horizontally apart: ``` L2 ["<<TABLE...L2 — Architecture>>"] subgraph L2A [""] ← design + explore (bidirectional, no planning crossing) subgraph L2B [""] ← planning (below design, via design→planning arrow) ``` This way `design ↔ explore` arrows stay within L2A's boundaries and don't enter L2B's space. The `design → planning` arrow exits L2A and enters L2B cleanly. Want me to apply this?
